A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BN-Pool research, with substantial overlap in the method and experiments. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support a reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-clustering and graph-classification experiments in Tables 1–2, together with qualitative analyses in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds graph-regression, heterophilic classification, sensitivity, and computational-resource results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: v2 Section 3.4.1 introduces a sparse BN-Pool variant that reconstructs observed edges and sampled nonedges instead of all node pairs, with normalization by their combined count. The reported dense auxiliary-loss normalization also changes from 1/N in v1 Equation 10 to 1/N² in v2 Equation 12. These change the training objective and computation while retaining the DP/SBM foundation.

E1.justification: v2 adds Peptides-struct graph regression and Multipartite classification under explicitly heterophilic, adversarial connectivity. These materially extend task and environmental coverage. The earlier datasets remain covered; GCB-H, IMDB, and DD results move to Appendix C, Table 12.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Table 2, v2 Tables 3 and 12 add evaluated graph-level comparators SEP, EigenPooling, and HOSC. Table 3 also adds a GNN without hierarchical pooling. The four node-clustering comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported graph-level settings change substantially: early-stopping patience falls from 500 to 100 epochs, learning-rate plateau patience from 200 to 30, and KL annealing from 300 to 50 epochs. MolHiv changes from one 32-unit MP layer before and after pooling to two 64-unit layers on each side with dropout and batch normalization. v2 also expands the prior-hyperparameter grid and introduces additional pooling-ratio evaluations.

E4.justification: v2 adds prior-hyperparameter sensitivity experiments on Enzymes and Colors3, comparator pooling-ratio sweeps, and analyses of memory, epoch time, and training duration, including dense versus sparse BN-Pool. Multipartite provides an explicit heterophilic stress test. The earlier Cora and GCB-H qualitative analyses are largely relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations. v2 newly specifies averaging over 10 folds for Table 5 and identifies dataset folds and weight initializations as sources of variation in Table 8. This adds limited statistical documentation; an increase in repetitions for retained results or a formal significance-testing procedure is not established.

E6.justification: The node-clustering scores are unchanged, but BN-Pool graph-level scores are revised: Colors3 changes from 93±1 to 99±0 and MUTAG from 91±8 to 88±7. Because reported settings also change, these are not controlled same-setting gains or losses. v2 adds substantial results, including Peptides-struct MAE of 0.255±0.001, Multipartite accuracy of 58±2, and new sensitivity, cluster-count, and resource measurements.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 3 restores the missing alpha_DP multiplier on the base-distribution term in v1 Appendix A, Equation 15, correcting the DP predictive distribution. Section 3.4.1 also supplies the sparse-loss expression and its 2E-term complexity argument. Most DP background and the underlying variational derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The central claim of the first adaptive soft-clustering pooling operator remains. The abstract shifts from broadly superior benchmark performance to preserving performance while producing compact representations. The conclusion extends the stated contribution to graph regression and sparse O(E) reconstruction, without replacing the principal adaptive-pooling claim.

C2.justification: v1 proposes heterophilic adaptation as future work; v2 documents underperformance on Multipartite and explains it through the model's homophilic architectural and loss biases. v2 also interprets hyperparameter sensitivity and explains dense/sparse memory and runtime tradeoffs, including reduced sampling efficiency as graph density increases. These substantially develop the applicability boundaries and limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset-specific selected hyperparameters in Table 11, hardware and timing information in Section 5.3, expanded forward-pass pseudocode, and GPU negative-sampling and dense-enumeration details in Appendix A. It also reports access through Torch Geometric Pool, supplementing the repository already linked in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting additional pooling comparators, broader graph applications, KL annealing, and software availability. However, Section 4 retains essentially the same positioning relative to DiffPool, DGVAE, SB-VAE, and the IBP-based overlapping SBM. Publication updates to existing references do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the introduction, adds an explicit contribution list, and divides the method into more explanatory subsections. Much of v1's DP background, model details, and qualitative-result discussion moves from appendices into the main text. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with widespread figure and table relocation. v2 adds overview and GNN/SRC diagrams, redraws the BN-Pool schematic, expands the cluster-distribution display, and introduces several analysis tables. The earlier graph-result table is split between the main text and appendix; retained qualitative figures are incorporated into the main presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation through additional comparators, a no-pooling control, pooling-ratio sweeps, an explicit heterophilic failure case, and measured dense/sparse computational costs. These address important gaps in v1's evidence, while dataset-specific settings and clearer exposition improve auditability. Changed protocols prevent attributing revised scores solely to method improvements, and sparse-variant task accuracy is not separately reported, but the broader controls and documented limitations provide a clear substantial net improvement.
